info.name: Smart Home - register devices
info.description:
Seeds the smart-home backend with the devices the mock vendors service knows: 3 vendors → 6 catalogue devices (with metric mappings) → 1 home → 6 home devices.

Run folders 1–4 in order (Collection Runner works). IDs are saved to collection variables automatically. Data already there? Run folder 0 first — it lists what exists and fills the id variables, so you can skip the register requests that would return 409.

Then: folder 5 reads and updates, 6 saves and queries readings, 7 creates and reads reports (daily and on-demand).

item.name: 0. What's already there
item.description: List endpoints. Each one also copies the ids of existing data into the collection variables, so after a 409 you can run this folder and carry on with folders 2–5 without resetting the DB.

exec: const mine = homes.find(h => h.name === "My home") || homes[0];
// Clear ids first, so a device that isn't registered in this database doesn't keep a stale id.

item.name: List home devices of my home
1. Vendors
item.description: Register the three mock vendors. Codes must match smarthome.vendors.<code> config.

item.name: 2. Catalogue devices (admin)
item.description: Supported models with metric mappings. Samsung payloads are nested, so their external metrics are dotted paths to the reading.

item.name: 4. Home devices (user)
item.description: The user's appliances; externalDeviceId must match a device id in the vendors service.

request.description: Replaces the full set of mappings (not a patch). Shows both styles: presets (conversion) and an explicit recipe (externalUnit/internalUnit/factor/offset + sample check).
internalUnit must be the metric's unit (POWER → W).
Reschedules nextRunAt to max(now, lastRunAt + interval). Allowed 60–86400 seconds.

item.name: 6. Device readings
item.description: Readings of the Bedroom AC: homeDeviceId, metric, time, value and unit (strings). unit is optional (defaults to the metric's unit). time = current minute; startDate/endDate = today (UTC), set by pre-request scripts.

request.description: One reading per device, metric and time.

item.name: 7. Reports
item.description:
Reports of the Bedroom AC (amz-ac-01).

DAILY reports are generated by the daily job for home-local days that ended at least 1 h ago (every 15 min; from the device's registration day, at most 7 days back). On-demand (CUSTOM_RANGE) reports are generated synchronously: POST returns 201 with the finished report. Full days come from the daily rollups, partial days and today from raw readings.

from/to are set by pre-request scripts. Run 'Create on-demand report' first: it saves reportId for Get / Regenerate.

item.name: Create on-demand report (last 24 h, all metrics)

request.description: metrics omitted → every metric the device's model maps.

item.name: Create on-demand report (last 7 days, ENERGY + TEMPERATURE, daily breakdown)

request.description: 7 UTC days up to the end of today. Each summary has a 'daily' list: total (energy kWh) or average (temperature) per home-local day.

exec: const to = new Date(); to.setUTCHours(0, 0, 0, 0); to.setUTCDate(to.getUTCDate() + 1);

request.description: The AC's model doesn't map HUMIDITY, so it never has readings for it.
Default window: the last 31 home-local days.
from/to are home-local ISO dates, both inclusive.

exec: const to = new Date(); to.setUTCHours(0, 0, 0, 0); to.setUTCDate(to.getUTCDate() + 1);

request.description: Recomputes the report from the current readings (e.g. after late data), same period and metrics. For a DAILY report the day's rollups are recomputed too.
